key_insight: CoRe-WM learns how breast MRI response states evolve during treatment, then uses frozen representations to predict pathologic complete response (pCR).
clinical_relevance: The approach could support research into treatment-response assessment during neoadjuvant chemotherapy, rather than relying on pretreatment imaging alone.
method: Predicts the next latent imaging state from longitudinal breast DCE-MRI.
Conditions state transitions on patient clinical profiles and assigned therapy, with a separate lesion-morphology response pathway.
Freezes pretrained model parameters and trains a linear pCR readout at each decision point.
evidence_signal: In five-fold cross-validation on I-SPY2, CoRe-WM reportedly achieved the highest discrimination among evaluated methods at every prospective decision point and showed cross-cohort transfer to I-SPY1.
watch_item: The abstract provides no numerical performance estimates or prospective clinical validation; this is treatment-response prediction research, not drug discovery or evidence for changing treatment.
paper_title: CoRe-WM: Conditioned Response-State World Modeling for Longitudinal Treatment-Response Prediction in Breast DCE-MRI
